name: Prelicensure RN clinical experiences
authority: NC Board of Nursing · 21 NCAC 36 .0321 · the NCCCS A45110 curriculum standard for a community college's ADN, the school's own plan of study for a university's BSN
edition: Starter content, 2026-10-28: the Board sets no minimum hour count per course or setting — the hours are the program's own course sessions; the experiences below are the lifespan settings a concept-based prelicensure curriculum places students in
summary: A North Carolina prelicensure RN program's clinical experiences are faculty-supervised (an instructor-led group of at most ten students, or a precepted experience directed by nursing faculty) across the lifespan: adult medical-surgical and critical care, maternal-newborn, pediatric, mental-health, older-adult / long-term care and community settings, closing with a precepted capstone in an adult acute setting. No state minimum hours apply per setting; the program's course sessions carry the hours and the ledger scores experiences as logged.

items.name: Adult medical-surgical nursing (acute inpatient)
items.notes: ADN: NUR 111, 112, 211; BSN: NSG 302, 426 — and the capstone's primary setting.

items.name: Critical care (ICU / CCU)
items.notes: ADN: NUR 212; BSN: NSG 426 — and the capstone where the site offers it.

items.name: Pediatric nursing (inpatient or ambulatory)
items.notes: ADN: NUR 113; BSN: NSG 314; a pediatric practice or clinic serves where no inpatient unit is within reach.

items.name: Long-term care / skilled nursing
items.notes: ADN: NUR 111's first clinical weeks; BSN: NSG 302's first clinical weeks.

items.name: Community, public-health, home-health or hospice nursing
Precepted practicum in an adult acute setting (1 student : 1 RN preceptor, directed by faculty)
items.notes: ADN: NUR 213 at 15 clinical hours a week; BSN: NSG 434 at 135 hours.
